    Where the data comes from

    Official government sources (accessed 14 Oct 2026)

    • Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA), via data.gov.sg: Amendment to Master Plan 2025 Land Use Layer (base map, coastline, zoning); Master Plan 2025 Planning Area Boundary (CCR, RCR and OCR frame); Master Plan 2025 Rail Station, Building (HDB blocks), SDCP Landed Housing Area, SDCP Urban Design Area (growth nodes) and Nature Reserve and National Park layers; Master Plan 2019 Land Use Layer (comparison only).
    • URA private residential transactions: Private Residential Property Transactions e-Service, all new sales, sub-sales and resales of condos and ECs from Oct 2021 to Oct 2026 (118,895 records). Used for every launch's price, sales and price growth. Locations from OneMap.
    • URA Government Land Sales: Past Sales Sites (updated 18 Sep 2026) and tender award announcements.
    • Housing & Development Board (HDB): Executive Condominium sites sold (26 Sep 2025) and EC site tender announcements.
    • HDB resale transactions: Resale flat prices from Jan 2017 (24,657 resales, Oct 2025 to Sep 2026, summarised by town).
    • Ministry of Education (MOE): General Information of Schools (all primary schools, SAP status).
    • Singapore Land Authority (SLA): OneMap (locations of schools and land-sale sites).

    Some figures, such as school ballot demand, school affiliations and the latest EC tender bids, also draw on third-party sources compiled by HuatNex. You may request this list from the founder separately should you need to find out more.

    Launch prices, sales and prices today are medians from URA's transaction records. Total unit counts for ten hand-researched launches, the upgrade rate, launch prices from before 2021, malls, job hubs and which stations are not yet open are HuatNex estimates. "Coming soon" assumes land won after mid-April 2025 has not launched yet.

    Guide

    How HuatNex works

    The one question we answer

    Is this new launch likely to have grown in value by the time you can sell it without the extra stamp duty?

    In Singapore, selling a private home within 4 years of buying it costs Seller's Stamp Duty. So we look ahead to that 4-year mark and ask whether the home is likely to be worth more by then, and whether there will be buyers ready to pay for it.

    How to use it

    1. Search. Type a launch, an area, an MRT station or a school into "Huat are you looking at?".
    2. Look at the map. See where it is and what's around it: schools, MRT stations, malls, growth areas and new homes being built nearby.
    3. Read the verdict. A Huat Score out of 100 and five plain answers, each with a coloured dot.
    4. Ask "Why?" Every answer opens up to show the reasons, and then the full workings if you want them.

    The map and the three market segments

    URA splits Singapore's private homes into three segments. They're drawn as thick outlines on the map:

    • CCR Prime core: Orchard, Newton, Bukit Timah, the city centre and Sentosa. The most expensive homes.
    • RCR City fringe: the rest of the central region, such as Toa Payoh, Queenstown and Kallang.
    • OCR Suburbs: everything outside the central region, such as Tampines, Ang Mo Kio and Woodlands. This is where executive condominiums (ECs) are built.

    Green bubbles show the buyer bank in each HDB town: the bigger and greener the bubble, the more families sold flats that had just passed their 5-year minimum occupation last year. These are the likeliest condo upgraders. Hover a bubble for its score out of 10.

    House-shaped markers show land the government has sold to developers. A filled marker means homes there are coming soon, usually 1 to 2 years after the land is sold. The segment counts at the top of the page are built from these land sales.

    The Huat Score

    The Huat Score rates a location out of 100 by mixing four ingredients. It ranks launches against each other. It is not a valuation or a probability.

    Schools
    Living within 1km of a primary school gives priority in the Primary 1 ballot, and families pay for that. Popular schools (oversubscribed in the Phase 2C ballot, or among the 50 most popular) count most, popular schools 1–2km away a little, and any other school within 1km a little.
    MRT
    Homes a short walk from a station hold value and rent more easily. A 5-minute walk scores highest. Planned stations count too, and we tell you when they're not open yet.
    Buyers
    Who could buy from you when you sell? Mostly families upgrading from HDB flats that have passed their 5-year minimum occupation. Half of this score comes from real HDB resale records for the area, and half from flats due to reach that 5-year mark around the time you'd sell.
    Few new condos
    Lots of new homes nearby means more competition for the same buyers. We count the homes on land sold to developers within 2km since 2021. The fewer there are, the higher the score.

    You can change how much each ingredient counts under "How does it compare with other launches?".

    How the five answers get their colours

    Question Green Amber Red
    Will there be buyers when you sell?At least 1 likely buyer for every 2 competing homes1 for every 2 to 4Fewer than 1 for every 4
    Good primary schools nearby?A popular school within 1kmOther schools within 1kmNo school within 1km
    Easy to get to an MRT?Within 500m500m to 1kmOver 1km
    Lots of new condos coming nearby?Few nearbySomeMany
    What could it sell for?15% or more above the launch price5% to 15%Under 5%

    The one-line takeaway follows the Huat Score: 75 or more is a strong location, 55 to 74 is decent with trade-offs, and below 55 is weaker.

    How we estimate the selling price

    We start from the launch price and grow it at the long-run price trend of its market segment (prime core, city fringe or suburbs): the average yearly growth of URA's price index over the last 10 and 12 years. We project 4 years ahead and show a middle case, a good case and a bad case. The Huat Score doesn't change the price forecast, because in testing it barely explained which launches did better.

    We also show the nearby launches of the same room type that grew the most since they launched, using URA's records of what buyers actually paid, and how many of their resales sold above or below the launch price. They are a cross-check, not the forecast.

    You choose a room type first, and every price is for that room type: the launch price, today's price and the similar launches we compare with. URA records floor area, not bedrooms, so we group units by size: 1-bedroom up to 600 sq ft, 2-bedroom 601–850, 3-bedroom 851–1,200, 4-bedroom 1,201–1,600, and 5-bedroom or penthouse above that. If fewer than two nearby launches have enough sales of that room type, we fall back to whole-project prices and say so.

    The price is before stamp duty, agent fees and loan interest, which all eat into your gain.

    How it did on past launches. We tested 17 launches from 2018 to 2022 whose 4-year mark has passed, including Clavon and Parc Clematis, using only what was known on launch day. Forecasting from the last 4 years of prices missed by about 10% in a typical case: too low for 2018–2020 launches, which caught the post-Covid boom, and too high for 2021–2022 launches. Using the last 10–12 years of prices, which is what this page now does, missed by about 4%, and 16 of the 17 forecasts landed within 10%. All 17 grew more slowly than their market segment's price index, by about 2 points a year, so buying at launch has carried a premium. Of 3,030 resales and sub-sales at these 17 projects since Oct 2021, 2,960 sold at least 5% above the launch price, 45 within 5% and 25 below it. Location scores barely explained which launches did better. These are early results from one market cycle.

    How sure are we?

    Wherever a figure appears in the workings, a small tag tells you how solid it is:

    Certain from official records or hard evidenceLikely a strong inference from good dataGuessing an estimate we still need to confirm

    Maps, zoning, MRT stations, schools, land sales, HDB resale prices and condo launch prices come from official records. Some unit counts and planning figures are still HuatNex estimates during this early preview.

    Where the data comes from

    Official sources from URA, HDB, MOE and SLA, listed under "Where the data comes from" below the map. Some figures, such as school ballot demand, also draw on third-party sources compiled by HuatNex. You may request this list from the founder separately should you need to find out more.

    What HuatNex is not

    • It is not a valuation, and the Huat Score is not a probability.
    • It is not financial advice. Speak to a licensed adviser before you buy.
    • Past price growth does not guarantee future growth, and interest rates, cooling measures and the wider economy can change the picture.
    • It is an early preview. For launches from late 2021 and 2022, whose 4-year window has passed, we now show what prices actually did next to our forecast. A full test of the scoring rules across all of them is next.
